scope: The complete set of entity type names registered by the Beta 1.7.3 client, and the entity-type mapping derived from it. This is registry existence, not natural-spawn lists: it establishes which entity types could exist at all, and therefore which spawn entries in a modern world are provably anachronistic.

source.method: Enumerate every printable string constant in jc.class. That class is the Beta entity name registry: it is the only class in the jar containing the known Beta mob names, and it also holds the non-mob entity names, the java.util.HashMap/reflection scaffolding and the register method. Reading the whole constant pool rather than searching for names I already suspected is what makes the list complete: a name I did not think of cannot be missed.

measuredAnachronisticSpawnEntries.observedSpawnLists: ambient={bat:10} creature={chicken:10, cow:8, pig:10, sheep:12, turtle:5, wolf:5} monster={creeper:100, enderman:10, skeleton:100, slime:100, spider:100, witch:5, zombie:95, zombie_villager:5} underground_water_creature={glow_squid:10} water_creature={squid:10}
measuredAnachronisticSpawnEntries.note: Every Beta-era mob Moderner Beta lists (chicken, cow, pig, sheep, wolf, squid, creeper, skeleton, spider, zombie, slime) is present in the Beta registry, so none of those is affected.

unknowns: Beta 1.7.3's own per-biome spawn weights and pack sizes are not enumerated here, so this establishes WHICH entity types may spawn, not the historical probability distribution.
Whether Moderner Beta's beta preset intends 1.7.3 or a slightly later Beta-era game remains the separate open question already recorded for emerald ore.
Spawn egg, breeding, spawner-block and mob-conversion paths are not natural spawning and are out of scope.
